texts: The main concern with retrograde cardioplegia through the coronary sinus is uneven distribution to the myocardium.
The right ventricle and the septum drain largely through veins that bypass the coronary sinus, so they receive little retrograde solution and may be poorly protected.
Retrograde delivery is therefore usually combined with antegrade cardioplegia.
Coronary sinus rupture, myocardial oedema and a persistent left superior vena cava are real but less common problems, managed by watching the line pressure and the anatomy.
